\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہدف} (hadaf)}{ہدف (hadaf)}]{\ur{ہدف} (hadaf) — a target; a goal}

\label{lesson:UR-C378-hadaf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to get worse, then the Urdu for to get better.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہدف}}
\textbf{\ur{ہدف}} — \emph{hadaf} — \textquotedblleft{}a target; a goal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ہدف} \ur{واضح} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{کام} \ur{آسان} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar hadaf vāzeh hai to kām āsān ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the target is clear, the work will be easier.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہدف}} (\emph{hadaf}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{hadaf}, \textquotedblleft{}a target, a mark aimed at\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hadaf}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hadaf}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar hadaf vāzeh hai to kām āsān ho gā.} — If the target is clear, the work will be easier.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to get worse, then the Urdu for to get better, then say \emph{hadaf} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ہدف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A target; a goal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عزم} (azm)}{عزم (azm)}]{\ur{عزم} (azm) — a resolve; determination}

\label{lesson:UR-C378-azm}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to get better, then the Urdu for a target.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عزم}}
\textbf{\ur{عزم}} — \emph{azm} — \textquotedblleft{}a resolve; determination\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{عزم} \ur{پختہ} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{کوئی} \ur{کام} \ur{مشکل} \ur{نہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar azm pukhtā hai to koī kām mushkil nahīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If your resolve is firm, no task is hard.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عزم}} (\emph{azm}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿazm}, \textquotedblleft{}resolve, determination\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to get better, then the Urdu for a target, then say \emph{azm} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قدم} (qadam)}{قدم (qadam)}]{\ur{قدم} (qadam) — a step}

\label{lesson:UR-C378-qadam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a target, then the Urdu for a resolve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قدم}}
\textbf{\ur{قدم}} — \emph{qadam} — \textquotedblleft{}a step\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ur{قدم}} (\emph{qadam}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qadam}, \textquotedblleft{}a foot; a step\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منصوبہ} (mansūbā)}{منصوبہ (mansūbā)}]{\ur{منصوبہ} (mansūbā) — a scheme; a plan (worked out)}

\label{lesson:UR-C378-mansuba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a resolve, then the Urdu for a step.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منصوبہ}}
\textbf{\ur{منصوبہ}} — \emph{mansūbā} — \textquotedblleft{}a scheme; a plan (worked out)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{منصوبہ} \ur{اچھا} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{حکومت} \ur{پیسے} \ur{دے} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar mansūbā achchhā hai to hukūmat paise de gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the scheme is good, the government will fund it.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منصوبہ}} (\emph{mansūbā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{manṣūba}, \textquotedblleft{}something set up, arranged\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}a plan\textquotedblright{} is the one Urdu uses.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mansūbā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mansūbā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar mansūbā achchhā hai to hukūmat paise de gī.} — If the scheme is good, the government will fund it.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a resolve, then the Urdu for a step, then say \emph{mansūbā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{منصوبہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A scheme; a plan (worked out)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حاصل} \ur{کرنا} (hāsil karnā)}{حاصل کرنا (hāsil karnā)}]{\ur{حاصل} \ur{کرنا} (hāsil karnā) — to achieve; to obtain}

\label{lesson:UR-C378-hasil-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a step, then the Urdu for a scheme.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حاصل} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{حاصل} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{hāsil karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to achieve; to obtain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{کوشش} \ur{کریں} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{ہدف} \ur{حاصل} \ur{کریں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp koshish kareṅ ge to hadaf hāsil kareṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you try, you will reach the target.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{ہدف} \ur{حاصل} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne hadaf hāsil kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حاصل} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{hāsil karnā}) is built from \emph{hāsil}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥāṣil}, \textquotedblleft{}resulting, obtained\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāsil karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāsil karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp koshish kareṅ ge to hadaf hāsil kareṅ ge.} — If you try, you will reach the target.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a step, then the Urdu for a scheme, then say \emph{hāsil karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{حاصل} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To achieve; to obtain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Danger and Damage to Setting a Goal}

\label{lesson:UR-R378-review-371-378}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for a crisis and poison.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a crisis, poison, deadly, to seep, to split open
  \item to freeze, to come to the boil, to soften in cooking, to crack, medium
  \item to scatter, to fade away, to tell off, to set (of the sun), unfinished
  \item someone to lean on, stubbornness, eligible, reliance, to insist
  \item very, extremely, thoroughly, tremendous, severe
  \item a count, an amount, minor, approximately, a limit
  \item worse, excellent, common, to get worse, to get better
  \item a target, a resolve, a step, a scheme, to achieve
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A crisis? (\textbf{\ur{بحران}}, \emph{buhrān}.) Poison? (\textbf{\ur{زہر}}, \emph{zahr}.) Deadly? (\textbf{\ur{جان} \ur{لیوا}}, \emph{jān-levā}.) To seep? (\textbf{\ur{رسنا}}, \emph{risnā}.) To split open? (\textbf{\ur{پھٹنا}}, \emph{phaṭnā}.) To freeze? (\textbf{\ur{جمنا}}, \emph{jamnā}.) To come to the boil? (\textbf{\ur{ابلنا}}, \emph{ubalnā}.) To soften in cooking? (\textbf{\ur{گلنا}}, \emph{galnā}.) To crack? (\textbf{\ur{تڑکنا}}, \emph{taṛaknā}.) Medium? (\textbf{\ur{درمیانہ}}, \emph{darmiyānā}.) To scatter? (\textbf{\ur{بکھرنا}}, \emph{bikharnā}.) To fade away? (\textbf{\ur{مٹنا}}, \emph{miṭnā}.) To tell off? (\textbf{\ur{ڈانٹنا}}, \emph{ḍānṭnā}.) To set (of the sun)? (\textbf{\ur{ڈھلنا}}, \emph{ḍhalnā}.) Unfinished? (\textbf{\ur{ادھورا}}, \emph{adhūrā}.) Someone to lean on? (\textbf{\ur{سہارا}}, \emph{sahārā}.) Stubbornness? (\textbf{\ur{ضد}}, \emph{zid}.) Eligible? (\textbf{\ur{اہل}}, \emph{ahl}.) Reliance? (\textbf{\ur{انحصار}}, \emph{inhisār}.) To insist? (\textbf{\ur{اصرار} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{isrār karnā}.) Very? (\textbf{\ur{بہت}}, \emph{bahut}.) Extremely? (\textbf{\ur{انتہائی}}, \emph{intihāī}.) Thoroughly? (\textbf{\ur{خوب}}, \emph{khūb}.) Tremendous? (\textbf{\ur{زبردست}}, \emph{zabardast}.) Severe? (\textbf{\ur{شدید}}, \emph{shadīd}.) A count? (\textbf{\ur{تعداد}}, \emph{tādād}.) An amount? (\textbf{\ur{مقدار}}, \emph{miqdār}.) Minor? (\textbf{\ur{معمولی}}, \emph{māmūlī}.) Approximately? (\textbf{\ur{لگ} \ur{بھگ}}, \emph{lag-bhag}.) A limit? (\textbf{\ur{حد}}, \emph{had}.) Worse? (\textbf{\ur{بدتر}}, \emph{badtar}.) Excellent? (\textbf{\ur{عمدہ}}, \emph{umdā}.) Common? (\textbf{\ur{عام}}, \emph{ām}.) To get worse? (\textbf{\ur{بگڑنا}}, \emph{bigaṛnā}.) To get better? (\textbf{\ur{سدھرنا}}, \emph{sudharnā}.) A target? (\textbf{\ur{ہدف}}, \emph{hadaf}.) A resolve? (\textbf{\ur{عزم}}, \emph{azm}.) A step? (\textbf{\ur{قدم}}, \emph{qadam}.) A scheme? (\textbf{\ur{منصوبہ}}, \emph{mansūbā}.) To achieve? (\textbf{\ur{حاصل} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{hāsil karnā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
